roundShape: Full round, as the architect named it: the merge 3760e51c resolves #2508's changes in runtime code this pull request rewrites (outbox/batch.go, outbox/publisher.go, internal/bus), and 14170450 changes internal/bus/async.go.

implementerProof.how: Re-ran the implementer's commands at 14170450 on a fresh UTF8 pod Postgres 17 database: bus package ok (355.8 s); TestARequestWhoseConnectionIsLostAnswersUnavailable -count=50 ok and CGO_ENABLED=1 -race -count=10 ok (10 of 10, no data race); outbox, duty and store ok; multiprocess ok (1070.3 s). With the fix reverted and the test hook called before the old synchronous flush, the test fails 3 of 3 with 'no answer within 10s' (window_request_test.go:175), so it pins the fix. Reverting async.go alone does not fail it, because the old code never calls the hook.

proof.criterion: INFRA-745's production scenario on the real binary at this head: five comments in quick succession on one issue routed to a session, under a grant with notifications.> withheld; each event's attempt_count, /metrics by reason, the ERROR lines, and the events behind the head publishing in order once the grant returns
proof.surface: real envoy-dispatch built at 14170450, as an nkey user of a real nats-server 2.10.29 whose publish permission is allow > deny notifications.>, changed by a configuration reload (SIGHUP) as an operator changes a grant; a second, ungranted connection subscribed to notifications.dispatch.issue.PV-1.> and notifications.agent.ses_p745 as the session; issue PV-1 routed to session:ses_p745
proof.command: natsr -c nats.conf (a copy of internal/testnats/cmd/natsd that reloads on SIGHUP); env NATS_NKEY_SEED_FILE=<seed> NATS_URLS=nats://127.0.0.1:14222 envoy-dispatch; five POST /api/v1/issues/PV-1/comments within 0.9 s; psql select id, attempt_count, published_at, published_destinations, next_attempt_at, publish_error from events; curl /metrics; then the grant restored by reload
proof.observed: Withheld, 40 s: event 4 (comment 1) attempt_count 4, publish_error 'bus: NATS denied the publish to "notifications.dispatch.issue.PV-1.comment.created" ...'; events 5-8 attempt_count 0, no error, next_attempt_at equal to event 4's (held behind it); /metrics envoy_dispatch_outbox_publish_failures_total{reason="denied"} 8 (4 attempts x 2 destinations), no failed or refused series. Every outbox ERROR line is msg="dispatch outbox: publish event" event_id=4 and names both subjects as 'NATS denied the publish to <subject>'; none says 'NATS is unreachable'. The session received nothing. Grant restored at 12:41:07.8Z: event 4 retried at its back-off (12:41:33.97Z, attempt 6) and all five published in one batch at 12:41:33.977Z, denied total 12 (6 x 2). On both subjects the session received event 4, 5, 6, 7, 8 (comment 1 to 5) in order, each envelope carrying quiet=false.
proof.negativeControl: The same scenario on main's own build at the merge base 88818a3b9b: every one of the five events was attempted (attempt_count 4 each after 40 s, denied 40, an ERROR line per event per attempt), and once the grant returned the session received comments 2-5 at 12:44:45.911Z and comment 1 twenty seconds later at 12:45:05.901Z: out of order. This head delivers comment 1 first.

proof.criterion: INFRA-745 acceptance 3 and this PR's per-issue order, both on that scenario
proof.observed: Met, with one difference from main for the reviewer to judge: a denied issue-topic publish is counted (reason="denied") and logged at ERROR naming the denied subject, and is retried, never dropped; the issue's later events wait behind it and publish in order once the grant returns. Unlike main, the events behind the head are not attempted while it is denied, so they get no attempt, no publish_error and no log line of their own, and the counter counts attempts of the head (2 per attempt here) rather than of every waiting event. On both builds the outbox's ERROR line comes 5 s after the server's violation (the ack wait), so that delay is main's too.
proof.negativeControl: main's build delivers comment 1 after comments 2-5 (above).

proof.criterion: #2508 in the batch model: quiet in every envelope; every send that did not reach NATS counted once
proof.surface: the real-binary run above, and the outbox package
proof.observed: Every envelope the session received (issue.created, issue.updated, five comment.created, on both subjects) carried quiet. The denied count was 2 per attempt of the head, matching its 6 ERROR lines across 2 destinations. TestEnvelopePayloadStatesWhetherTheEventIsQuiet, TestRunRetriesAnIssueTopicNATSDenies, TestRunCountsEveryDeniedJetStreamDestinationOfOneEvent, TestRunCountsADeniedSubjectOncePerRefusedMessage (on two issues) and TestAPublishFailureThatEndsTheAttemptIsCountedOnce pass; outbox ok 399.2 s, duty ok 45.6 s, store ok 416.2 s.
proof.negativeControl: Main's build on the same denial counted 40 against this head's 8 at the same moment, because it attempts every event (above).

proof.criterion: One publisher, take-over within 10 s, each session takes each event once and in order
proof.surface: two real envoy-dispatch processes on one Postgres and one NATS (multiprocess harness)
proof.command: cd packages/envoy && DISPATCH_TEST_DATABASE_URL=<fresh pod database> go test -p 2 -parallel 4 -tags multiprocess -count=1 -timeout 40m -v ./cmd/dispatch
proof.observed: ok 1070.3 s, peak memory 2.93 GB. Take-over 5.1 s after SIGKILL, 3.0 s after a NATS cut, 2.3 s after a silent cut, 4.4 s after SIGSTOP; the resumed process logged the hold lost 4 ms after it resumed; the watcher took 200 comments, the role's holder 80, the thread's author 60, each once and in order. A first run in a background job was ended by SIGHUP from outside at 12:56:33Z with no test failed; this foreground run replaces it.
proof.negativeControl: TestAFrozenPublisherSendsNothingWhenItResumes: the SIGSTOPped holder sent nothing after it resumed.
